narrative.overview:
Painted flowers frame fine calligraphic names and headings, with formal serif event details on cream paper. Pale botanical sage, a photographic woodland field, and a lilac venue field carrying blush stationery express the user-pinned floral reference. Open lists and restrained controls keep guest information readable. This system belongs only to the Mario & Inah invitation.

The opening photograph is immediately visible and leads directly into the floral countdown. Supplied floral cutouts and the botanical pattern remain recognizable artwork; they are not approximated with CSS. Couple photographs remain samples in client data and provenance, with one gallery-level disclosure. There are no per-image watermark overlays. The venue uses the actual uploaded Panaad Garden photograph.

Hero corner flowers use -bottom-2 on both sides, -left-2 on the left and -right-2 on the right, without translation transforms. Countdown corner flowers shift outward by 25% of their width and use bottom-5 with no vertical translation. Entourage corner flowers shift outward by 25% of their width and use bottom-3 with no vertical translation. Both photo breaks fill at least one dynamic viewport height with full-bleed cover images; responsive image sizes account for their landscape source aspect ratio.

The hero cycles through four configured sample photographs with a 900ms fade and 6.5-second reading interval. Names, date and corner flowers remain fixed. Only the first photo loads initially; each next photo is mounted when requested and decoded before replacing the current image. Controls support pause/play, direct selection and left/right arrow keys. Focused selection pauses autoplay. Offscreen and hidden-tab playback stops; reduced motion disables autoplay and uses instant manual changes. With JavaScript disabled the first photo remains visible and controls are omitted.

Gentle parallax is limited to hero/photo-break backgrounds and floral cutouts: spring-smoothed scroll movement, half-distance on phones, fixed reading content and controls, safe photo overscan, and immediate reduced-motion fallback. See components/ParallaxLayer.tsx and README.md for the bounded distances.

Hero controls are four small circular dots without a background or pause/play icons. Dot selection pauses autoplay; the active dot offers accessible pause/resume, with keyboard navigation and reduced-motion support preserved.

Entourage refinement: larger 16–18px serif names, clear 12px role labels, an understated geometric hairline divider after the parents, framed principal sponsors, and paired columns that stack below 360px. Supplied florals, sage paper and all confirmed names are retained.

Each section now has first-entry content motion: resolving calligraphy, brief text-group rises, slow photographic settling and a fine divider opening. One observer triggers each element once; default HTML is visible. Live reduced motion settles ongoing animation and disables new reveals. These content effects remain separate from slideshow fades and background parallax.

The user requested an image welcome screen: a full-viewport, configured photograph with ivory names/date, supplied butterfly florals and an Open invitation link. It precedes the slideshow hero in normal document flow. JavaScript enhances the anchor with smooth scrolling and heading focus; reduced motion is instant and the native no-JavaScript link remains usable. Only immediately visible welcome assets are prioritized.

Slideshow cadence is now three seconds, with a slow 3% photo zoom over the active display plus crossfade. The plain dot controls remain unchanged; zoom follows pause, offscreen and hidden-tab behavior and is disabled with reduced motion.

The latest requested opening supersedes the earlier scroll-only welcome: a progressively enhanced photo cover with restrained framing, independent staggered lettering and flowers, slow photo drift, and a 750ms dissolve into a ready hero. Invitation content enters after the cover lettering clears. Behind-cover content remains inert until completion, and temporary scrolling restrictions are restored. Direct guest-detail links and the native no-JavaScript flow remain available, with reduced-motion and image-readiness fallbacks.

The refined welcome stacks Mario and Inah in ivory Imperial calligraphy, separated by a smaller Libre Baskerville ampersand. A fine hairline and diamond divider sits beneath the confirmed date, and a transparent outlined Open invitation action completes the composition. The names enter in a restrained stagger; short-height screens scale the lettering down while keeping the action visible. The existing photo drift, floral exit and cover dissolve remain intact.

Text entrances emphasize the wedding names: the welcome lettering softly resolves from 2px blur with an 18px rise and 220ms name stagger, followed by its date and location. Section calligraphy resolves over 900ms from 25% opacity and a 14px rise; supporting text uses a quieter 700ms fade and 10px rise. Entourage names animate individually with a short row stagger capped at 200ms, while role labels stay separate. The hero title animates its inner lettering without moving keyboard focus. Content remains visible by default and animations run once, settle on interruption, and honor live reduced-motion preferences.
keyCharacteristics: Fine calligraphy, formal serif event details and quiet sans-serif controls.
Cream paper, botanical sage, woodland photography and lilac with blush stationery.
Painted floral overlaps and a directly readable photographic opening.

rules.name: The Surface and Swatch Rule
rules.body: Preserve the supplied section grounds independently of attire suggestions.

rules.name: The Calligraphic Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Keep Imperial Script for names and headings, formal serif for event details, and sans-serif for controls and longer prose.

rules.name: The Botanical Depth Rule
rules.body: Let artwork, photographs and tonal surfaces supply depth; keep content cards and controls flat.

dos: Do keep client-specific styles, artwork, configuration and design records inside this invitation folder.
Do use Tailwind for ordinary layout and scoped CSS for typography and layered decoration.
Do preserve supplied artwork, actual venue photography, the gallery sample disclosure and readable photo text.
Do preserve keyboard focus, direct section links and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep confirmed content data-driven and pending information explicit.
donts: Don't substitute attire suggestions for the supplied section grounds.
Don't replace the direct photographic opening with a cover or entry gate.
Don't add elevated cards, competing layout declarations or decorative substitutes for supplied artwork.
Don't represent prepared email drafts as recorded or sent RSVPs.
Don't invent couple photographs, story text, a playable music asset or names for pending entourage roles.
